label: Residues
notes: Open the chapter. The residue calculus on one complex variable extends to higher dimensions through multivariate residues, the Grothendieck residue symbol, the global residue theorem, and the Cousin problems. The deck follows printed pages 647 through 732. The chapter is the analytic-side toolkit for global complex-geometric computations.

label: One-Variable Residue
notes: Recall the one-variable residue. For a meromorphic one-form on a Riemann surface, the residue at a point is the coefficient of dz over z minus a in a local Laurent expansion. The global residue theorem on a compact Riemann surface states that the sum of residues of any meromorphic differential is zero.

label: Grothendieck Residue
notes: Define the Grothendieck residue. For a meromorphic n-form on an n-dimensional manifold with an isolated zero of the denominator at a point, the residue is given by an integral over a small real n-torus. The symbol is multilinear and behaves well under base change. It provides the higher-dimensional analog of the Laurent coefficient.

label: Residue Theorem
notes: State the global residue theorem in several variables. For a compact complex manifold and a meromorphic n-form with isolated poles, the sum of all Grothendieck residues equals zero. This is the higher-dimensional analog of the curve sum-of-residues vanishing and produces nontrivial relations among local data.

label: Cousin Problems
notes: Cover the Cousin problems. The first Cousin problem asks whether prescribed principal parts of a meromorphic function can be globally realized; the second asks the same for divisor data. Solvability is controlled by sheaf cohomology vanishing. On Stein manifolds and on suitably positive projective varieties, the problems have positive answers.

label: Applications
notes: Walk through applications. Residue methods recover trace formulas for direct images, intersection number computations via local Grothendieck residues, and the explicit form of the Riemann-Roch theorem in low dimensions. Residues package transcendental analytic data in a way that is compatible with algebraic constructions.

label: Recap
notes: Close the chapter. One-variable residues generalize to Grothendieck residues; the global residue theorem extends the curve identity; Cousin problems are governed by sheaf cohomology vanishing; applications include trace formulas and intersection-theoretic computations. The next chapter focuses on a concrete classical object, the quadric line complex.
